marrow__ANAT_CH41_Q002.takeaway: Costosternal articulation occurs through costal cartilage, whereas costovertebral, costotransverse and costochondral joints directly involve a rib.
marrow__ANAT_CH41_Q002.displayText: The costosternal joint is not formed by direct articulation of a rib with the sternum; it is formed by articulation of the lateral sternal border with the costal cartilage. Costovertebral and costotransverse joints directly involve ribs, and the costochondral joint is at the rib-costal cartilage junction.

rationales.a: The rib head articulates with vertebral bodies at the costovertebral joint.
rationales.b: The rib-to-cartilage junction is the costochondral joint.
rationales.c: The rib tubercle articulates with the transverse process at the costotransverse joint.

Pancoast tumors can destroy the first rib by mass effect.
